title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
summary: Combine two sorted arrays into one sorted array in linear time.
statement:
Given two integer arrays `a` and `b`, each sorted in **non-decreasing** order, return a single new
array that contains every element of both, also in non-decreasing order.

Don't just concatenate and call `Arrays.sort`: aim for O(n + m) time.
constraints: a and b are each sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: Both inputs are already sorted. Which two elements are the only candidates for the smallest remaining value?
Keep one index into each array. Repeatedly copy the smaller front element into the result, then copy whatever is left over once one array runs out.

result = new int[a.length + b.length]
i = 0, j = 0, k = 0
while i < a.length and j < b.length:
    if a[i] <= b[j]: result[k++] = a[i++]
    else: result[k++] = b[j++]
copy the rest of a, then the rest of b
return result

This is the merge step of merge sort. Each element is copied exactly once: O(n + m) time and O(n + m) space for the output. Using `<=` (rather than `<`) takes from `a` on ties, which keeps the merge stable. Forgetting the leftover tail after one array is exhausted is the most common bug.
